title: Module comparison: original Mel Filter Bank and final SkewDCT branch

rows.original: Custom RTL first-order pre-emphasis and shift-register framing. A coefficient is assigned inside the module.
rows.current: Reworked custom RTL with parameterized Q15 pre-emphasis, previous accepted raw sample, signed arithmetic and PCM16 saturation.
rows.notes: Modified upstream stage. Sample history advances on accepted input. Frame output holds under backpressure. The input frame remains register-based.

rows.original: Custom RTL multiply with an embedded N-word cyclic coefficient register. Changing N requires regenerated source coefficients.
rows.current: Custom RTL Q14 window multiplication. A coefficient file supplies eight length-dependent rows, selected for N=16..2048.
rows.notes: Extended upstream window stage to all eight lengths and deterministic reload. Active coefficients still rotate in registers; this stage is not described as fully BRAM-based.

rows.original: FFT arithmetic is internal to XFFT IP. No standalone FFT16 RTL root is provided in upstream.
rows.current: Integrated custom RTL FFT16 arithmetic root with registered fixed-angle operations. It forms the 16-point root family and is also reused inside FFT256.
rows.notes: Custom RTL integration/adaptation. The shared FFT system supports 16/32/64/128/256/512/1024/2048. Size scheduling, twiddle lookup, buffers and control are implementation details, not extra counted modules.

rows.original: No standalone FFT256 RTL root. Transform stages are implemented inside XFFT IP.
rows.current: Integrated custom RTL two-pass FFT16-based FFT256 transform, including its intermediate rotation and fixed-point scaling.
rows.notes: Reused for 256/512/1024/2048 processing. Root-local buffers, CNORM, the shared radix-4 merge and point-selection wrappers are included here or in FFT2x remarks rather than counted separately.

rows.original: No custom real/imaginary packing and reconstruction module. Real data is supplied to the configured complex XFFT IP.
rows.current: Custom RTL real/imaginary packing, conjugate-pair splitting and spectrum reconstruction around the shared complex FFT result.
rows.notes: Handles 32/128/512/2048 real-point extensions. Cache RAMs and the shared radix-2 merge belong to this block. AMD Radix-4 Burst I/O starts at 64 points; other XFFT architectures also support 16/32 [S2].

rows.original: RTL wrapper around XFFT IP and two mult_gen_0 multiplier IP instances. The packaged square multipliers have seven pipeline stages.
rows.current: Custom RTL real/imaginary square products followed by a registered magnitude sum, with aligned valid/last signals.
rows.notes: Replaced mult_gen_0 multiplier IP with pipelined RTL arithmetic. The surrounding FFT stream wrapper is not counted. In the MFCC top, N is fixed at elaboration; the standalone FFT top supports runtime size selection.

rows.original: 40 Mel outputs, a cyclic coefficient register, ascending/descending accumulation and one mult_gen_1 multiplier IP.
rows.current: Rewritten custom RTL 64-band sparse lookup. Each frequency-bin entry contains up to two band IDs and Q15 weights. Two 48-bit products feed 64-bit energy sums.
rows.notes: Replaced multiplier IP and coefficient rollover logic. Registered operand selection, products and accumulation align tags. Invalid-band sentinel 127 suppresses writes; short FFTs can leave empty bands.

rows.original: Custom dB_LUT uses a large combinational casex table and integer dB outputs. It is not an IP core.
rows.current: Custom RTL floor clamp, leading-one detection, normalized mantissa lookup in a 1024-entry Q20 ROM, exponent correction and Q8 output conversion.
rows.notes: Replaced the active integer dB case table with a 1024-entry Q20 mantissa lookup, exponent correction and Q8 output. Added a floor and size-aware scaling. Tagged arithmetic stages improve timing; controllers and lookup storage are not separate rows.

rows.original: Absent. There is no custom or IP-based DCT core in the original project.
rows.current: Custom RTL recursive 8-to-4-to-2 skew transform for eight coefficient families, with Q21 constants and a 13-stage tagged pipeline. One shared core handles eight groups.
rows.notes: Combines the skew arithmetic core and its TDM use. Input permutation, the 3-bit family selector, normalization, registers and scheduling are included. The factorized expression uses 12 real products and 29 add/subtract operations, not 12 measured DSPs.

rows.original: Absent. No ordinary DCT8 bank is present.
rows.current: Custom RTL ordinary DCT8 transform shared across eight groups. Its factorized arithmetic core uses a nine-stage tagged pipeline.
rows.notes: DCT8 arithmetic, TDM scheduling, normalization and result reordering are one block in this table. Multiplication and add/subtract stages are registered separately; buffers and controllers are not additional modules.

rows.original: Absent. There is no DCT post-processing or cepstral output ordering stage.
rows.current: Custom RTL arithmetic combines and reorders the eight-point transform results into the 64-point DCT output.
rows.notes: Includes the pipelined operand selection, optional compensation product and final post-add. These are stages of one arithmetic block. Together with SkewDCT8 and DCT8 TDM, it implements the 64-point DCT.

rows.original: Custom RTL output packing for 40 16-bit Mel values, with OUT_WIDTH dividing 40.
rows.current: Adapted RTL gathers and formats 64 cepstral coefficients, 26 bits each at default precision, for serial or parallel output.
rows.notes: Changed 40 Mel outputs to 64 DCT coefficients. MFCC integration, coefficient assembly, lane selection and ready/valid/TLAST control are included, without separate wrapper or controller rows.

granularity: 12 major algorithm/processing blocks. FFT16/FFT256/FFT2x/SkewDCT8/DCT8 TDM define the minimum transform granularity. Wrappers, memories and controllers are folded into notes.
ip_note: Custom RTL means no packaged XFFT, DCT or multiplier IP in the production datapath; DSP/BRAM primitive inference is still allowed.
